Good topic for work English. Today's goal: add -s or -es to the verb after he, she and it.
Quick reminder: after I, the verb stays the same, as in "I work."
Now think of a colleague you know well. Write one sentence about what that person does in a normal workday. Start with "He" or "She".
I will give feedback on your sentence and one clear next step.

Quick reminder: regular past verbs usually end in -ed, as in "I visited a friend."
First task: write two short sentences about what you did last weekend, or on your last day off.
I will give feedback on the exact words you use and one next step.

Yes! Let's start with time. Use "at" with clock times, not "in".
Right: "The game starts at 9 o'clock." Wrong: "The game starts in 9 o'clock."
Your turn. Write one sentence: when does your school start? Use 8 o'clock.

[[assess verdict=NOT_EVALUATED relevance=NO_ACTIVE_ITEM next=NEW_ITEM]]
Hi! Let's meet a family. Say "This is my" before the family word.
Right: "This is my father." Wrong: "This is father." It has no "my".
Your turn. Write one sentence about your mother. Start with "This is my".
s2030_P2_r1:
[[assess verdict=NOT_EVALUATED relevance=NO_ACTIVE_ITEM next=NEW_ITEM]]
Hi! When people change a time, the last time is the answer.
Right: A: "Meet at four?" B: "No, at five." The time is five. Wrong: four. B changed it.
Your turn. A: "Class at two?" B: "No, at three." What time is the class?

Right: "This is a book." Wrong: "This is a bag" when you hold a book. It is not a bag.

Hi! Look. One cat: "There is a cat." Two cats: "There are two cats." So use "is" for one and "are" for more than one.
Right: "There are two dogs." Wrong: "There is two dogs."
Your turn. Write is or are: "___ two birds in the tree."

Right: "Yesterday I cooked rice." Wrong: "Yesterday I cook rice."
Your turn. Finish the sentence: "Yesterday we ___ (jump) in the park."

Your turn. Write in, on or at: "My class ends ___ 3 o'clock."
